discovery: Development of controlled/living radical polymerization (atom transfer radical polymerization and RAFT) for precise synthesis of functional polymers
rationale: Controlled radical polymerization changed how polymers are made in industry and in the lab. It allows precise control of chain length, architecture and functionality, and it underpins materials used in coatings, medicine and electronics. These scientists have long been named as likely winners in citation-based forecasts. Recent prizes went to biology-adjacent work (2024, protein design) and to framework materials (2025, MOFs), so the committee could turn next to synthetic polymer chemistry, a core area of chemistry.
